Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

violent adjective

also violently, fierce, rough (of the sea), violence

classical

Cic. Phil. 5.19: homo vehemēns et violentus (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 34.32.3: tyrannus saevissimus et violentissimus in suōs (Lewis & Short)
Gell. 19.1.1
Traupman 159, 402

violentus, violenta, violentum

violent, forcible, boisterous

Of people, tempers and rule, and of wind, rivers and the sea (Lucr., Verg.). Violence itself is vīs (see force).

Other words

  • vehemēns, vehementis — vehement, impetuous, fierce

    also used · classical · Cic. Vat. 4: vehemēns ferōxque nātūrā (Lewis & Short)

    Eager and forceful rather than brutal; of an orator it can be praise (Cic. Brut. 88). Often written vēmēns (Ter., Catull., Lucr.).

  • violentia, violentiae f. — violence, vehemence

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 159, 402

  • ferōx, ferōcis — fierce, high-spirited

    also used · classical · Traupman 314

Examples

  • nāvigābāmus ā Cassiopā Brundisium mare Īonium violentum et vāstum et jactābundum

    we were sailing from Cassiope to Brundisium over the Ionian sea, violent, vast and heavingGell. 19.1.1

See also force, strongly.
